claim: JD Sports cut JD Germany from 91 stores (start FY27) to a core estate of 62 (completed August 2026, after period-end) and reorganised the German head office with job cuts. JD Europe H1 FY27 LFL was -5.1% (revenue -1.0% cc to GBP1,104m) in a 'leisure footwear market in decline'. JD Europe operating profit after lease interest still rose 80%, helped partly by the Germany head-office and store rationalisation. JD Europe ended flat at 689 stores (16 opened, 16 closed).
data_point: JD Germany 91->62 (-29, -32%); JD Europe H1 FY27 (26 wks to 2026-08-01) LFL -5.1%, revenue GBP1,104m (-1.0% cc), op. profit after lease interest +80%; 689 stores flat
source_name: JD Sports Fashion plc HY27 Results Statement
original_quote: JD Germany consolidated from 91 to 62 stores (completed post period -end) ... JD Europe revenue fell -1.0% at constant FX rates to £1,104m ... alongside a -5.1% reduction in LFL sales ... the leisure footwear market in decline
verifier_note: Verified in the PDF text: 91->62, GBP1,104m, -5.1% LFL, 'leisure footwear market in decline', +80% operating profit and the 689-store table. Caveat: the +80% also reflects gross margin and own-brand apparel, not only the German cuts. The baseline already has JD Europe LFL by quarter from JPM (Q1 FY27 -4.2%, Q2E -6.0%), so the H1 LFL is incremental; the German cut and the profit payoff are new.

claim: JD is moving its smaller Eastern European markets to a franchise with Sport Vision. Over 40 JD stores in six markets will run as Sport Vision franchises, and Sizeer's operations in five markets (over 30 stores) will move to Sport Vision; Poland is unaffected. CEO Schultz says these markets were at roughly break-even and will now earn franchise profit, with store assets sold to Sport Vision ('more localisation, fewer assets'). His criteria are market size, operating complexity and access to property. Exit charges were small: about GBP9m tied to the disposals, plus GBP9m of store-impairment reversals from early lease exits.
data_point: ~70 stores transferred (analyst figure on the call); GBP9m charges for the Eastern European disposal (statement is internally inconsistent: GBP8m goodwill + GBP1m Croatia loss in the notes vs GBP9m goodwill in the summary; the Croatia note shows a GBP0.1m net loss); GBP9m impairment-reversal credits from early exits and lease terminations
source_name: JD HY27 analyst presentation transcript (Regis Schultz) + HY27 Results Statement
original_quote: we were, I would say, at break-even in those countries. So, we will make a profit where we were at break-even ... more localisation, fewer assets, a focus on key markets
verifier_note: The transcript quote, the criteria (size, complexity, property) and the '70 stores are getting transferred' analyst question are verified. The statement confirms 40+ JD stores in 6 markets, Sizeer in 5 markets with 30+ stores, and Poland unaffected. Correction to the scraper: the charge split differs between sections of the same statement (see data_point). This is a JD precedent, not an FL action.

claim: JD CEO Schultz, answering a question on promotions: 'our key competitor made the wrong assumption that everything would be rosy by September. We have been proved right.' JD's CFO expects the promotional, overstocked environment to continue through H2, and JD's view of European market growth is unchanged. The scraper cites a paywalled Times snippet saying Schultz blamed competitors 'such as Foot Locker' for overstocking. I could not verify that snippet.
data_point: Sneakers now 55-60% of the footwear market, so no return to double-digit growth; H2 promotions and stock levels unchanged vs H1; JD's Europe/UK market view unchanged, North America weaker
source_name: JD HY27 analyst call; The Times 2026-09-23 (paywalled, unverified)
original_quote: our key competitor made the wrong assumption that everything would be rosy by September. We have been proved right.
verifier_note: The quote, the 55-60% figure, CFO Platt's 'expect that to continue through the second half' and 'our view on Europe and the UK is unchanged' are all verified in the transcript. The transcript has zero mentions of 'Foot Locker'. The FL attribution rests only on The Times snippet, which I could not retrieve (paywall; web search and Apify budgets exhausted). Downgraded to B because the FL link is unconfirmed.

claim: Courir (owned by JD) is expanding in Italy, FL's largest European market. It grew to 8 Italian stores in H1 FY27, targets 18 by year-end and has a long-term goal of 100. Group-wide, Courir went from 313 to 324 stores (+12 opened, -1 closed), and JD calls the French market 'challenging'.
data_point: Courir Italy 8 stores -> 18 target by FYE -> 100 long-term; Courir 313->324 stores in H1 FY27
original_quote: Italy is Courir's priority country for growth, with the business growing to eight stores in the half and targeting 18 by year-end, with a longer-term objective of 100 stores across the country
verifier_note: Quote and store table verified. Tier B: 8-18 stores is small against FL's Italian estate. Its relevance is the competitive trend, not a near-term shock.

claim: Price brackets for a European sneaker-chain sale. Courir (profitable) sold to JD for EV EUR520m, about 0.72x 2023 sales of EUR726m and about 10x EBIT of EUR50.3m. Footasylum was sold under a CMA order for GBP37.5m to Aurelius in 2022, roughly 0.13x sales. Frasers offered NOK10/share for the rest of loss-making XXL. Inference: a loss-making FL Europe would price at the distressed end, which favours licensing or closure over a value sale.
data_point: [d] Courir EV/sales 0.72x, EV/EBIT ~10.3x; Footasylum GBP37.5m (sales multiple uses scraper's ~GBP281m, unverified); XXL NOK10/sh, ~GBP17m for remaining shares per FashionUnited
original_quote: JD Sports buys Courir for €520 million, 10 times EBIT
verifier_note: Courir EUR520m, EUR726m sales, EUR50.3m EBIT and 323 stores are verified on MIND. Footasylum GBP37.5m to Aurelius (2022-07-29) is verified on FashionUnited. XXL NOK10/share (~GBP17m) is verified; XXL revenue NOK7.18bn and Footasylum sales were not verified. The baseline already has Evercore's EV/EBITDA precedents (e.g. Frasers/Accent 3.7x), but not these European sales multiples. The conclusion about FL Europe's value is inference.

claim: AGAINST (Italy): Italian shopping-centre sales rose 2.2% and footfall rose 1.8% in H1 2026, with apparel +2.2% (CNCC-EY Observatory). Mall traffic in FL's largest European market is not collapsing. Inference: FL Italy's problem is competition and promotions, not footfall.
data_point: Italian malls H1 2026: sales +2.2%, footfall +1.8%, apparel +2.2%; 70% of retailers expect sales growth next year
source_name: EY Italia / CNCC Osservatorio press release
verifier_note: Verified on the EY page (Milan, 30 Jul 2026), including sales +2.2%, footfall +1.8% and Abbigliamento +2.2%. This is mall-wide data, not sneaker or FL data. The inference about the cause of FL Italy's weakness is the scraper's.

claim: German retail is shrinking. The HDE trade association forecasts a net loss of about 4,900 shops in 2026, to about 296,600. Regional press counted only 60 stores on JD's German store list on 7 Aug 2026, against 88 in an archived June-2026 list. Named closures: Herne, Kiel, Krefeld, Muelheim-Kaerlich, Wiesbaden, Zwickau (closed 1 Aug) and Jena (clearance sale to 22 Aug).
original_quote: Doch es scheint nicht rundzulaufen in Deutschland
english_translation: But things don't seem to be running smoothly in Germany
verifier_note: Both pages verified. Downgraded to C: the JD Germany part duplicates finding 1 (JD's own 91->62 disclosure), and the HDE figure covers all German retail, not sneakers. The article also notes that a ~30-store JD Germany cut was reported in May 2025 (Immobilien Zeitung).

claim: Nike Q1 FY27 prepared remarks (2026-10-01): aged, higher-volume Sportswear footwear sold through below expectations, which 'impacted our future order books' with wholesale partners. Nike will cut the volume and frequency of specific Jordan retro launches. Supply cuts will weigh on revenue for the rest of FY27 and into FY28. Dunk revenue was cut by nearly 50% (about a $200m headwind), and EMEA revenue fell 5%. Nike says North America will feel the biggest near-term impact.
data_point: Sportswear down low double digits; Dunk ~-50% (~$200m); EMEA -5% (currency-neutral); Q2 laps EMEA Cyber Week promotions (~400bp revenue headwind combined with NA sell-in comparison)
source_name: NIKE Inc. Q1 FY27 prepared remarks
original_quote: some aged, higher-volume Sportswear footwear sold-through below expectations. Looking ahead, that has impacted our future order books as we proactively work with our wholesale partners to work through excess inventory
verifier_note: All quotes verified in the PDF (dated October 1, 2026). Downgraded to B: Nike says 'North America will feel the biggest impact', and the baseline already has a Deutsche Bank EMEA channel check (2026-07-22) on reduced Nike order books. The EMEA DTC/wholesale split from the 10-Q was not verified.

claim: Australia, FL's main APAC market, shows the same stress. Accent Group FY26: H2 LFL -2.0% (H1 +0.9%), gross margin 53.1% vs 54.9% on a 'heightened promotional environment', 59 stores closed, A$48.6m goodwill impairment and a statutory NPAT loss of A$13.8m. Frasers' all-cash offer of A$0.65/share (about A$390m, roughly 0.26x owned sales) was extended to 2026-09-30. Accent's Sports Direct ANZ rollout expects 8 stores plus online by Dec-2026.
data_point: Accent owned sales A$1.53bn (+4.7%); underlying EBIT A$105.3m; reported EBIT A$34.0m; [d] A$0.65 x 601.2m shares = ~A$391m
source_name: Accent Group FY26 results (ASX:AX1); Frasers RNS 'Update on Offer for Accent'
original_quote: LFL sales in H1 were up 0.9% and in H2 were -2.0%. Q4 FY26 was materially impacted by the escalation of geopolitical tensions and a significant deterioration in consumer confidence.
verifier_note: All figures verified in the ASX PDF and the Investegate RNS. Correction: Sports Direct ANZ is run by Accent under a retail agreement with Frasers, not by Frasers directly. Tier B: Accent is a peer, not FL. The baseline has Frasers' 2024 minority stake in Accent, but not the 2026 full bid.

claim: Romania's Competition Council is reviewing BDS RO Sport SRL's (Sport Vision) takeover of MIG Marketing Investment Group RO SRL, the JD Sports Group unit that runs Sizeer and JD Sports in Romania. Combined 2025 sales would approach RON1bn: Sport Vision Romania RON525m (+21%), MIG RO ~RON390m (+6%).
data_point: BDS RO Sport 2025 sales RON525m (+21%); MIG RO ~RON390m (+6%); deal value undisclosed
original_quote: Consiliul Concurenţei analizează tranzacţia prin care BDS RO Sport SRL intenţionează să preia MIG Marketing Investment Group RO SRL
english_translation: The Competition Council is analysing the transaction by which BDS RO Sport SRL intends to take over MIG Marketing Investment Group RO SRL
verifier_note: The regulator review is verified on Wall-Street.ro; the revenue figures are verified on ZF. Same transaction as finding 2 (country-level detail), so this is corroboration rather than a separate precedent. The scraper's quoted phrase 'trebuie autorizata' was replaced with the verified sentence.

claim: Licensing economics: Fourlis, FL's SE-Europe licensee, plans 8-10 new Foot Locker stores a year. Management says a new store breaks even in year one, earns about 5% operating profit in year two and 8-10% when mature. Counter-signal: MoneyBuzz (2026-09-13) reports that 'one or two Foot Locker stores are under review' in Romania within Fourlis' ~10 planned 2026 closures.
data_point: 8-10 FL openings/yr; break-even yr1, ~5% EBIT yr2, 8-10% mature; 1-2 Romanian FL stores under review
source_name: Edison Group initiation on Fourlis (Russell Pointon, 2026-07-30); MoneyBuzz.gr (Cristian Hatis, 2026-09-13)
original_quote: A new store typically breaks-even in the first year and generates an operating profit of 5% in the second year before reaching a margin of 8-10% when mature
verifier_note: Both sources verified with dates. Edison is issuer-sponsored research relaying management targets, not results, so tier B. The baseline has the Fourlis licence and the '>100 stores' ambition but not these unit economics. The chatter file mentions 'up to 12 new licensed stores' (unverified), which is not the same fact.

claim: Adidas CEO Gulden (H1-2026 report): the lifestyle-shoe market, especially men's, is under pressure because many retailers are discounting heavily, 'above all in Europe'. Puma Q2 footwear fell 11.7%. Asics performance running grew 19.3% in H1. IFH Koeln/BBE expect German shoe spending to fall a third straight year, to EUR9.3bn in 2026 (2025: ~EUR9.4bn).
data_point: German shoe market ~EUR9.4bn (2025) -> EUR9.3bn (2026E); Puma Q2 footwear -11.7%; Asics performance running +19.3% H1, SportStyle +83%
original_quote: Der Markt für Lifestyle-Schuhe, insbesondere im Herrensegment, steht derzeit unter Druck, weil viele Händler stark reduzieren – vor allem in Europa
english_translation: The lifestyle-shoe market, especially men's, is under pressure because many retailers are discounting heavily, above all in Europe
verifier_note: The SZ quote and figures and the TW market sizing are verified. Cuts against: the baseline has adidas Q2-2026 Europe +8% (JPM), so the brand itself grew in Europe. Sector context, not FL-specific, so tier B.

claim: Spain precedent: Intersport Espana, a buying centre and brand for a sports-store network, went into liquidation in 2025. The brand, buying centre and part of the staff went to Intersport France for EUR300,000, the only bid for that lot (court approval pending at publication). The store network was split into up to 14 mostly regional lots. Nike and Puma were among the creditors.
data_point: EUR0.3m for brand + buying centre; up to 14 store lots; in insolvency since March 2025
original_quote: se ha hecho con la marca y parte de los trabajadores de la empresa por 300.000 euros
english_translation: has acquired the brand and part of the company's workforce for EUR300,000
verifier_note: Verified on Modaes. Downgraded to C: it is a 2025 event, a buying-group structure rather than an owned sneaker chain, and the court approval was still pending at publication. The '~120 stores' figure was not verified, and the EUR300k does not price the store network.

claim: Rivals are adding capacity in FL's core EU markets. Frasers agreed to take majority control of Italy's Maxi Sport (18 stores, premium multi-sport) on 2026-02-05 and plans to launch Sports Direct in Italy 'in the future'. Sports Direct opened a ~32,000 sq ft Helsinki flagship (Jun-2026). JD Spain is reported heading to 138 stores by early 2027.
data_point: Maxi Sport 18 IT stores; Helsinki ~32,000 sq ft; JD Spain ~134->138 (unverified)
original_quote: grow Maxi Sport's unique offering and also launch Sports Direct in Italy in the future
verifier_note: Maxi Sport and Helsinki are verified. JD Spain 138 rests only on the URL slug (Cloudflare 403). REFUTED sub-claim: the Snipes x PSG release is dated 23 Sept 2024 (only reposted on the newsroom in Aug-2026), so it is not a 2026 push and was removed. Maxi Sport is premium multi-sport/winter, not sneaker; the scraper's 'sneaker formats' detail was not verified. Courir Italy duplicates finding 4.

claim: Zalando narrowed its 2026 guidance (2026-08-04) to GMV and revenue growth in the lower half of its previous 12-17% range. Its B2C adjusted EBIT fell to EUR164.1m from EUR173.7m. Reuters and Investing.com snippets attribute the weakness mainly to sneakers (low-double-digit % of GMV).
data_point: Growth in the lower half of 12-17%; adj. EBIT guide EUR680-720m (from EUR660-740m); B2C adj. EBIT EUR164.1m vs EUR173.7m
source_name: Zalando Q2-2026 release; Reuters / Investing.com (snippets, blocked)
original_quote: now expects, on a reported basis, GMV and revenue growth in the lower half of its previous 12% to 17% range in line with market expectations
verifier_note: The guidance and EBIT figures are verified on Zalando's own page. The release does not mention sneakers, and it says the narrowing was 'in line with market expectations', which cuts against a shock framing. The sneaker attribution and the 'record fall' could not be verified (Reuters 401, Investing 403). Tier C.

claim: AGAINST (Japan): FL is still spending on atmos Tokyo flagships. Foot Locker atmos Japan relocated 'atmos pink flagship Harajuku' within Harajuku and reopened it with a new concept on 2026-07-04. atmos SHIBUYA was refitted and reopened on 2025-10-04.
data_point: Harajuku relocation/reopening 2026-07-04 (PR dated 2026-06-26); Shibuya renewal reopening 2025-10-04 (closed from end-Aug 2025)
source_name: PR TIMES (Foot Locker atmos Japan GK)
original_quote: 「atmos pink flagship Harajuku」店が、2026年7月4日(土)より同エリア内にて移転・リニューアルオープンいたします
english_translation: atmos pink flagship Harajuku will relocate within the same area and reopen with a renewal from Saturday 4 July 2026
